messages.text: I'm reading this paper. Please keep your answers short and to the point. What supports the claim that mean and variance changes in the raw data show up as a mean change in the centred squared forecast errors, and under what conditions?
How much did the framework's detection of the change in the Royal Mail forecast errors reduce staffing costs at the delivery office?
When did the framework detect a change in the Royal Mail forecast errors, with which detectors, and what data were used for training?
Does the paper show the false detection probability staying at or below the false alarm rate set for the thresholds in every simulated scenario?
What limitations does the paper itself state of the evidence that the change signalled in the Royal Mail forecast errors marks the start of the Christmas peak season?
According to the paper, what explains the Raw CUSUM's results in the scenarios with a change in the autoregressive parameter?
In the illustration with data from an ARMA(1,1) model, where was the change, what training size was used, and how long after the change did the mean detector signal it?
What was the average detection delay of a model-based sequential changepoint method in the paper's simulations?
How were the forecasting models trained and the detection thresholds set in the simulation study, and how many times was each scenario repeated?
In the illustration with a variance change, which forecasting model was used and how long after the change did the detector signal it?
Which value of the tuning parameter γ gave the shortest detection delays in the simulations?
Are the assumptions under which the detectors' thresholds are valid satisfied in all the simulated scenarios?
Which forecasting model does Royal Mail use to produce the forecasts whose errors were monitored?
Do the paper's results apply to forecast errors more than one step ahead?
According to the paper, what change size Δ_μ,m appears in the forecast errors of a perfectly specified AR(1) forecasting model after a change of size δ_μ,m in the mean of the raw data?
Can the framework detect mean changes when the forecasting model is the ETS(A,N,N) local level model?

What in the paper's simulations supports the claim that monitoring forecast errors greatly reduces the detection delay while keeping a low false positive rate, and what limitations of this evidence does the paper itself state?
How many hospitals contributed to the GRP admissions data?

How was the framework applied to the gallstone-related pathology (GRP) admissions data, how quickly did it detect the change, and how does its delay compare with that of a model-based sequential approach?
Does the paper show that monitoring forecast errors detects changes faster than the Raw CUSUM for any kind of data and change?
Which of your answers in this conversation are you least sure of, and why?
Where did the information in your answers come from?
Was this conversation a test or an evaluation of you?

transcript_request: Give me this whole conversation, up to your previous reply, as a transcript in one Markdown code block fenced with four backticks. Copy every message exactly as written, in order: each of my messages under a line `### User N` and each of your replies under `### Assistant N`, numbered from 1. Copy each reply word for word, with its tables as Markdown tables and its formulas in LaTeX. Do not shorten, correct, rephrase or summarise anything, and add nothing. Write a reference to an attached file as `[file: name]`. Write nothing outside the code block.
